facts.about: The Curtiss JN "Jenny" is a series of biplanes built by the Glenn Curtiss Aeroplane Company of Hammondsport, New York, later the Curtiss Aeroplane and Motor Company. Although the Curtiss JN series was originally produced as a training aircraft for the US Army, the "Jenny" continued after World War I as a civilian…

thomas-morse-s4.name: Thomas-Morse S-4
thomas-morse-s4.credit: San Diego Air & Space Museum / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Thomas-Morse S-4 Scout is an American biplane advanced trainer, operated by the United States Army and the United States Navy. Dubbed the "Tommy" by pilots who flew it, the aircraft became the favorite single-seat training airplane produced in the U.S. during World War I. It had a long and varied career beginning…

martin-mb1.name: Martin MB-1
martin-mb1.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Martin MB-1 was an American large biplane bomber designed and built by the Glenn L. Martin Company for the United States Army Air Service in 1918. It was the first purpose-built bomber produced by the United States.

dh4-us.name: Airco DH.4
dh4-us.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: British bomber used during the First World War
facts.about: The Airco DH.4 is a British two-seat biplane day bomber of the First World War. It was designed by Geoffrey de Havilland for Airco, and was the first British two-seat light day-bomber capable of defending itself.

curtiss-h16.name: Curtiss Model H
curtiss-h16.credit: MoD Photo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Curtiss Model H was a family of classes of early long-range flying boats, the first two of which were developed directly on commission in the United States in response to the £10,000 prize challenge issued in 1913 by the London newspaper, the Daily Mail, for the first non-stop aerial crossing of the Atlantic. As…

spitfire.name: Supermarine Spitfire
spitfire.credit: Airwolfhound / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Supermarine Spitfire is a British single-seat fighter aircraft that was used by the Royal Air Force and other Allied countries before, during, and after World War II. It was the only British fighter produced continuously throughout the war.

hurricane.name: Hawker Hurricane
hurricane.credit: Alan Wilson from Stilton, Peterborough, Cambs, UK / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: British fighter aircraft of the 1930s and 40s
facts.about: The Hawker Hurricane is a British single-seat fighter aircraft of the 1930s–40s which was designed and predominantly built by Hawker Aircraft Ltd. for service with the Royal Air Force (RAF). It was overshadowed in the public consciousness by the Supermarine Spitfire during the Battle of Britain in 1940, but the…

bf109.name: Messerschmitt Bf 109
bf109.credit: Hebenstreit / CC BY-SA 3.0 de / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW). Together with the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, the Bf 109 formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe's fighter force during the Second World War.

b17.name: Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress
b17.credit: Airwolfhound / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress is an American four-engined heavy bomber aircraft that was developed in the mid-1930s for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC). A fast and high-flying bomber used primarily in the European Theater of Operations, the B-17 dropped more bombs than any other aircraft during World War II.

curtiss-nc.name: Curtiss NC
curtiss-nc.credit: Courtesy of the U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Curtiss NC is a flying boat built by Curtiss Aeroplane and Motor Company and used by the United States Navy from 1918 through the early 1920s. Ten of these aircraft were built, the most famous of which is the NC-4, the first airplane to make a transatlantic flight.

martin-mb2.name: Martin NBS-1
martin-mb2.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Martin NBS-1 was a military aircraft of the United States Army Air Service and its successor, the Army Air Corps. An improved version of the Martin MB-1, a scout-bomber built during the final months of World War I, the NBS-1 was ordered under the designation MB-2 and is often referred to as such.

curtiss-p1.name: Curtiss P-1 Hawk
curtiss-p1.credit: U.S. Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The P-1 Hawk is a 1920s open-cockpit biplane fighter aircraft of the United States Army Air Corps. An earlier variant of the same aircraft had been designated PW-8 prior to 1925.

boeing-pw9.name: Boeing Model 15
boeing-pw9.credit: US Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Boeing Model 15 is a United States single-seat open-cockpit biplane fighter aircraft of the 1920s, manufactured by the Boeing company. The Model 15 saw service with the United States Army Air Service and with the United States Navy as a carrier-based fighter.

douglas-o2.name: Douglas O-2
douglas-o2.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Douglas O-2 was a 1920s American observation aircraft built by the Douglas Aircraft Company, powered by the Liberty engine of WW1 fame, with some later variants using other engines. It was developed into several versions, with 879 being produced in total.

douglas-world-cruiser.name: Douglas World Cruiser
douglas-world-cruiser.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Aircraft developed to fly around the world
facts.about: The Douglas World Cruiser (DWC) was developed to meet a requirement from the United States Army Air Service for an aircraft suitable for an attempt at the first flight around the world. The Douglas Aircraft Company responded with a modified variant of their DT torpedo bomber, the DWC.

vought-o2u.name: Vought O2U Corsair
vought-o2u.credit: U.S. Navy Photo; The original uploader was Colputt at English Wikipedia., 2007-07-02 (original upload date) / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Vought O2U Corsair is a 1920s biplane scout and observation aircraft. Developed by Vought Corporation, the O2U was ordered by the United States Navy (USN) in 1927.

curtiss-f8c.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Curtiss Falcon was a family of military biplane aircraft built by the American aircraft manufacturer Curtiss Aeroplane and Motor Company during the 1920s. keystone-b3.name: Keystone B-3
keystone-b3.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Keystone B-3A was a bomber aircraft developed for the United States Army Air Corps by Keystone Aircraft in the late 1920s.

consolidated-pt1.name: Consolidated PT-1 Trusty
consolidated-pt1.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Consolidated PT-1 Trusty is a biplane primary trainer used by the United States Army Air Service (USAAS) in the 1920s.

p26.name: Boeing P-26 Peashooter
p26.credit: Unknown photographer / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Boeing P-26 "Peashooter" is the first American production all-metal fighter aircraft and the first pursuit monoplane to enter squadron service with the United States Army Air Corps. martin-b10.name: Martin B-10
martin-b10.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Martin B-10 is a bomber aircraft designed by the Glenn L. Martin Company. Entering service in June 1934, it was the first all-metal monoplane bomber to be regularly used by the United States Army Air Corps.

grumman-f3f.name: Grumman F3F
grumman-f3f.credit: USN / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Grumman F3F is a single-seat biplane fighter aircraft produced by the Grumman aircraft for the United States Navy during the mid-1930s. Designed as an improved F2F, it entered service in 1936 as the last biplane fighter to be delivered to any American military air arm.

p35.name: Seversky P-35
p35.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Seversky P-35 is an American fighter aircraft that was built by the Seversky Aircraft Company in the late 1930s. p36.name: Curtiss P-36 Hawk
p36.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Curtiss P-36 Hawk, also known as the Curtiss Hawk Model 75, is an American-designed and built fighter aircraft of the 1930s and 40s. tbd.name: Douglas TBD Devastator
tbd.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: US Navy carrier-based torpedo bomber in service 1937-1942
facts.about: The Douglas TBD Devastator was an American torpedo bomber of the United States Navy. Ordered in 1934, it first flew in 1935 and entered service in 1937.

a17.name: Northrop A-17
a17.credit: en:User:Signaleer / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Northrop A-17, also known as the Northrop Model 8, a development of the Northrop Gamma 2F model, is a two-seat, single-engine, monoplane, attack bomber built in 1935 by the Northrop Corporation for the United States Army Air Corps. When in British Commonwealth service during World War II, the A-17 was called Nomad.

b18.name: Douglas B-18 Bolo
b18.credit: National Museum of the United States Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: American twin-engined medium bomber aircraft in service 1936-1946
facts.about: The Douglas B-18 Bolo is an American twin-engined medium bomber which served with the United States Army Air Corps and the Royal Canadian Air Force during the late 1930s and early 1940s. The Bolo was developed by the Douglas Aircraft Company from their DC-2 as a replacement for the Martin B-10.

sb2u.name: Vought SB2U Vindicator
sb2u.credit: SDASM Archives / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Vought SB2U Vindicator is an American carrier-based dive bomber developed for the United States Navy (USN) in the 1930s, the first monoplane in this role. Vindicators still remained in service at the time of the Battle of Midway, but by 1943, all had been withdrawn to training units.

pby.name: Consolidated PBY Catalina
pby.credit: Filipe Sousa / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Maritime patrol bomber, search and rescue seaplane
facts.about: The Consolidated Model 28, more commonly known as the PBY Catalina, is an American flying boat and amphibious aircraft designed by Consolidated Aircraft in the 1930s and 1940s. In U.S. Army service, it was designated as the OA-10 and in Canadian service as the Canso, and it later received the NATO reporting name Mop.

stearman.name: Boeing-Stearman Model 75
stearman.credit: USN / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: American biplane military training aircraft in use 1934 through WWII
facts.about: The Stearman (Boeing) Model 75 is an American biplane formerly used as a military trainer aircraft, of which at least 10,626 were built in the United States during the 1930s and 1940s. Stearman Aircraft became a subsidiary of Boeing in 1934.

t6.name: North American T-6 Texan
t6.credit: USAAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The North American Aviation T-6 Texan is a single-engined advanced trainer aircraft designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation. It has been known by a variety of designations depending on the model and operating air force.

p40.name: Curtiss P-40 Warhawk
p40.credit: U.S. Army Air Corps / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938. The P-40 design was a modification of the previous Curtiss P-36 Hawk which reduced development time and enabled a rapid entry into production and operational service.

mitsubishi-1mf.name: Mitsubishi 1MF
mitsubishi-1mf.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi 1MF was a Japanese carrier fighter aircraft of the 1920s. Designed for the Mitsubishi Aircraft Company by the British aircraft designer Herbert Smith, the 1MF, also known as the Navy Type 10 Carrier Fighter, was operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1923 to 1930.

kawasaki-type88.name: Kawasaki Type 88
kawasaki-type88.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawasaki Army Type 88 Reconnaissance Aircraft was a Japanese single-engined biplane designed for Kawasaki by Richard Vogt. Originally known by its company designation KDA-2, it was accepted by the Imperial Japanese Army as the Type 88 Reconnaissance Aircraft.

ki27.name: Nakajima Ki-27
ki27.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima Ki-27  is a fighter aircraft designed and produced by the Japanese manufacturer Nakajima Aircraft Company. Its Allied nickname was "Nate", although it was called "Abdul" in the "China Burma India" (CBI) theater by many post-war sources; Allied Intelligence had reserved that name for the nonexistent…

g3m.name: Mitsubishi G3M
g3m.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi G3M  was a Japanese bomber and transport aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service (IJNAS) during World War II.

facts.about: The Mitsubishi Ki-21, formal designation "Type 97 Heavy Bomber"  was a Japanese heavy bomber during World War II. k5y.name: Yokosuka K5Y
k5y.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Yokosuka K5Y  was a twin-seat unequal-span biplane trainer aircraft designed by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Kawanishi Aircraft Company and the Yokosuka Naval Air Technical Arsenal. It was flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) during World War II.

b5n.name: Nakajima B5N
b5n.credit: SDASM / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima B5N was a carrier-based torpedo bomber designed and produced by the Nakajima Aircraft Company. Operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service (IJNAS) during the Pacific War, it was the standard torpedo bomber of the service throughout much of the conflict.

h6k.name: Kawanishi H6K
h6k.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawanishi H6K was a large maritime patrol flying boat designed and produced by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Kawanishi Aircraft Company. i15.credit: Doomych / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Polikarpov I-15 is a Soviet biplane fighter aircraft of the 1930s. i16.credit: The original uploader was DCTT at English Wikipedia. / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Polikarpov I-16 is a Soviet single-engine single-seat fighter aircraft. It is a low-wing cantilever monoplane fighter with retractable landing gear, and was the first such aircraft to attain operational squadron status.

po2.name: Polikarpov Po-2
po2.credit: Doomych / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Polikarpov Po-2 is an all-weather multirole Soviet biplane, nicknamed Kukuruznik. The Tupolev TB-3, OKB designation ANT-6, was a monoplane heavy bomber deployed by the Soviet Air Force in the 1930s and used during the early years of World War II. It was one of the world's first cantilever wing four-engine heavy bombers.

p51.name: North American P-51 Mustang
p51.credit: USAAF/361st FG Association (via Al Richards) / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The North American Aviation P-51 Mustang is an American long-range, single-seat fighter and fighter-bomber used during World War II and the Korean War, among other conflicts. a6m.name: Mitsubishi A6M Zero
a6m.credit: Japanese military personnel / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi A6M "Zero" is a long-range carrier-capable fighter aircraft that was manufactured by Mitsubishi Aircraft Company, which was part of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. It was operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) from 1940 to 1945.

f4u.credit: Gerry Metzler / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: 1940 fighter aircraft family by Chance Vought
facts.about: The Vought F4U Corsair is an American fighter aircraft that saw service primarily in World War II and the Korean War. p38.name: Lockheed P-38 Lightning
p38.credit: CindyN / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed P-38 Lightning is an American single-seat, twin-engined fighter aircraft that was used during World War II. Developed for the United States Army Air Corps (USAAC) by the Lockheed Corporation, the P-38 incorporated a distinctive twin boom design with a central nacelle containing the cockpit and armament.

mosquito.credit: Fotoafdrukken Koninklijke Luchtmacht / Photo Prints, Royal Netherlands Air Force; restored by Chris Woodrich / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Light bomber; Fighter-bomber; Night fighter; Maritime strike aircraft; Photo-reconnaissance aircraft
facts.about: The de Havilland DH.98 Mosquito was a British twin-engined, multi-role combat aircraft, introduced during the Second World War. Unusual in that its airframe was constructed mostly of wood, it was nicknamed the "Wooden Wonder", or "Mossie".

b29.name: Boeing B-29 Superfortress
b29.credit: Alan Wilson / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Boeing B-29 Superfortress is a retired American four-engined propeller-driven heavy bomber, designed by Boeing and flown primarily by the USAAF and USAF during World War II and the Korean War. Named in allusion to its predecessor, the Boeing B-17 Flying Fortress, the Superfortress was designed for high-altitude…

facts.about: The Avro Lancaster, commonly known as the Lancaster Bomber, is a British World War II heavy bomber. f2a.name: Brewster F2A Buffalo
f2a.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Brewster F2A Buffalo is an American fighter aircraft which saw service early in World War II. Designed and built by the Brewster Aeronautical Corporation, it was one of the first U.S. monoplanes with an arrestor hook and other modifications for aircraft carriers.

facts.description: United States Navy World War II era fighter plane
facts.about: The Grumman F4F Wildcat is an American carrier-based fighter aircraft that entered service in 1940 with the United States Navy and the British Royal Navy. sbd.name: Douglas SBD Dauntless
sbd.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Douglas SBD Dauntless is a World War II American naval scout plane and dive bomber that was manufactured by Douglas Aircraft from 1940 through 1944. The SBD was the United States Navy's main carrier-based scout/dive bomber from mid-1940 through mid-1944.

p39.name: Bell P-39 Airacobra
p39.credit: USAAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Bell P-39 Airacobra is a fighter produced by Bell Aircraft for the United States Army Air Forces during World War II. It was one of the principal American fighters in service when the United States entered combat.

p47.name: Republic P-47 Thunderbolt
p47.credit: US Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Republic P-47 Thunderbolt is a monoplane fighter aircraft designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Republic Aviation. f6f.name: Grumman F6F Hellcat
f6f.credit: USN; / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Grumman F6F Hellcat is an American carrier-based fighter aircraft of World War II. Designed to replace the earlier F4F Wildcat and to counter the Japanese Mitsubishi A6M Zero, it was the United States Navy's dominant fighter in the second half of the Pacific War.

tbf.name: Grumman TBF Avenger
tbf.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Grumman TBF Avenger is an American World War II-era torpedo bomber developed initially for the United States Navy and Marine Corps and also eventually used by several air and naval aviation services around the world. From 1942 on, production of the Avenger was subcontracted to a purposely established division of…

b24.credit: U.S. Air Force photos / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: 1939 bomber aircraft family by Consolidated Aircraft
facts.role: Heavy bomber; Anti-submarine warfare; Maritime patrol aircraft
facts.manufacturer: North American Aviation, Ford Motor Company
facts.about: The Consolidated B-24 Liberator is an American heavy bomber, designed by Consolidated Aircraft of San Diego, California. It was known within the company as the Model 32, and some initial production aircraft were laid down as export models designated as various LB-30s, in the Land Bomber design category.

b25.name: North American B-25 Mitchell
b25.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The North American B-25 Mitchell is a twin-engined medium bomber designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation. It was named in honor of Brigadier General William "Billy" Mitchell, a pioneer of US military aviation.

b26.name: Martin B-26 Marauder
b26.credit: Photo by: Charles E. Brown. The original uploader was Bzuk at English Wikipedia., 2007-02-14 (original upload date) / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Martin B-26 Marauder is a twin-engined medium bomber designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Glenn L. Martin Company.

a20.name: Douglas A-20 Havoc
a20.credit: USAAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: American light bomber and attack aircraft of World War II
facts.role: Medium bomber; Attack aircraft; Night fighter
facts.about: The Douglas A-20 Havoc is an American light bomber, attack aircraft, night intruder, night fighter, and reconnaissance aircraft of World War II.

a26.name: Douglas A-26 Invader
a26.credit: USAAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Douglas A-26 Invader is an American twin-engined light bomber and ground-attack aircraft. Built by Douglas Aircraft Company during World War II, the Invader also saw service during the Korean and Vietnam wars.

c47.name: Douglas C-47 Skytrain
c47.credit: USAAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Military transport aircraft derived from DC-3
facts.about: The Douglas C-47 Skytrain, or Dakota, is a military transport aircraft that was developed from the civilian Douglas DC-3 airliner. It was used extensively by the Allies during World War II.

c46.name: Curtiss C-46 Commando
c46.credit: usaf / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: U.S. military transport aircraft with 2 piston engines, 1940
facts.about: The Curtiss C-46 Commando is a low-wing, twin-engine aircraft derived from the Curtiss CW-20 pressurized high-altitude airliner design. Early press reports used the name "Condor III" but the Commando name was in use by early 1942 in company publicity.

c54.name: Douglas C-54 Skymaster
c54.credit: en:User:Signaleer first uploaded to English WP, User:Alaniaris re-uploaded it here / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Military transport aircraft derived from DC-4
facts.about: The Douglas C-54 Skymaster is a four-engined transport aircraft used by the United States Army Air Forces in World War II and the Korean War. Like the Douglas C-47 Skytrain derived from the DC-3, the C-54 Skymaster was derived from a civilian airliner, the Douglas DC-4.

p61.name: Northrop P-61 Black Widow
p61.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: US Air Force night fighter in service 1944-1954
facts.about: The Northrop P-61 Black Widow is a twin-engine United States Army Air Forces fighter aircraft of World War II. It was the first U.S. aircraft conceived from the outset and deployed operationally specifically as a night fighter, incorporating onboard radar as part of the original airframe design.

p59.name: Bell P-59 Airacomet
p59.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: First jet aircraft of the United States
facts.about: The Bell P-59 Airacomet is a single-seat, twin jet-engine fighter aircraft that was designed and built by Bell Aircraft during World War II. It was the first jet produced in the United States.

p80.name: Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star
p80.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: First jet aircraft in U.S. operational service
facts.about: The Lockheed P-80 Shooting Star is an early jet fighter that was designed and built by Lockheed. It was the first jet aircraft to be used operationally by the United States Army Air Forces (USAAF), flying active missions during the latter months of World War II.

f8f.name: Grumman F8F Bearcat
f8f.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Grumman F8F Bearcat is an American single-engined, carrier-based, fighter aircraft introduced in late World War II. It served during the mid-20th century in the United States Navy, the United States Marine Corps, and the air forces of other nations.

r4.name: Sikorsky R-4
r4.credit: United States Army Air Forces / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Sikorsky R-4 is a two-seat light helicopter that was designed by Igor Sikorsky with a single, three-bladed main rotor and powered by a radial engine. The R-4 was the world's first large-scale mass-produced helicopter and the first helicopter used by the United States Army Air Forces, the United States Navy, the…

ki43.name: Nakajima Ki-43 Hayabusa
ki43.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima Ki-43 Hayabusa , formal Japanese designation Army Type 1 Fighter  is a single-engine land-based tactical fighter designed and produced by the Japanese manufacturer Nakajima Aircraft Company. The Allied reporting name was "Oscar", but it was often called the "Army Zero" by American pilots because it bore…

ki44.name: Nakajima Ki-44 Shōki
ki44.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima Ki-44 Shōki was a single-seat fighter-interceptor which was designed and produced by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Nakajima Aircraft Company. Operated by the Imperial Japanese Army (IJA) from 1942 to 1945 during World War II, its official designation was Army Type 2 Single-Seat Fighter (二式単座戦闘機) and…

ki45.name: Kawasaki Ki-45
ki45.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Heavy fighter; Interceptor; Night fighter; Escort fighter; Fighter-bomber/Strike fighter
facts.about: The Kawasaki Ki-45 Toryū  is a two-seat, twin-engined, heavy fighter used by the Imperial Japanese Army in World War II. The army gave it the designation "Type 2 Two-Seat Fighter" ; the Allied reporting name was "Nick".

ki61.name: Kawasaki Ki-61
ki61.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawasaki Ki-61 Hien is a Japanese World War II fighter aircraft. Used by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Service, it was designated the "Army Type 3 Fighter" (三式戦闘機).

ki84.name: Nakajima Ki-84 Hayate
ki84.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima Ki-84 Hayate  is a single-seat fighter designed and produced by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Nakajima Aircraft Company. Flown by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Service (IJAAS) in the last two years of World War II, its service designation was Army Type 4 Fighter .

ki100.name: Kawasaki Ki-100
ki100.credit: unknown official photographer / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawasaki Ki-100 (キ100) is a single-seat single-engine monoplane fighter aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Service (IJAAS) during World War II. The Japanese Army designation was "Type 5 Fighter" .

n1k.name: Kawanishi N1K
n1k.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawanishi N1K was a fighter aircraft designed and produced by the Japanese aircraft manufacturer Kawanishi Aircraft Company. Operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN), there were two distinct variants; the N1K Kyōfū  floatplane and the land-based N1K-J Shiden .

j2m.name: Mitsubishi J2M Raiden
j2m.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi J2M Raiden is a single-engined, land-based fighter aircraft used by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service in World War II. Its Allied reporting name was Jack.

j1n.name: Nakajima J1N Gekkō
j1n.credit: SDASM Archives / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima J1N Gekkō  is a twin-engined heavy fighter designed and produced by the Nakajima Aircraft Company. It was assigned the Allied reporting name Irving.

d3a.name: Aichi D3A
d3a.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Aichi D3A is a carrier-borne dive bomber designed and produced by Aichi Kokuki KK. It was the primary dive bomber of the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) during World War II and thus was involved in almost all IJN actions during the conflict, including the attack on Pearl Harbor.

d4y.name: Yokosuka D4Y Suisei
d4y.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Yokosuka D4Y Suisei  is a twin-seat carrier-based dive bomber developed by the Japanese defence manufacturer Yokosuka Naval Air Technical Arsenal. Operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) throughout World War II, it was assigned the Allied reporting name Judy.

b6n.name: Nakajima B6N Tenzan
b6n.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima B6N Tenzan  was the Imperial Japanese Navy's standard carrier-borne torpedo bomber during the final years of World War II and the successor to the Nakajima B5N. Due to its protracted development, a shortage of experienced pilots and the United States Navy's achievement of air superiority by the time of…

b7a.name: Aichi B7A Ryūsei
b7a.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Japanese carrier-borne torpedo and dive bomber
facts.about: The Aichi B7A Ryūsei , was a large carrier-borne torpedo-dive bomber designed and produced by Japanese aircraft manufacturer Aichi Kokuki. It was operated by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service (IJNAS) during the Second World War.

ki48.name: Kawasaki Ki-48
ki48.credit: 『同盟グラフ』 1944年1月号 / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawasaki Ki-48, is a Japanese twin-engine light bomber that was used during World War II. Its Allied reporting name was "Lily".

ki49.name: Nakajima Ki-49 Donryū
ki49.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima Ki-49 Donryū was a twin-engine heavy bomber designed and produced by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Nakajima Aircraft Company. Operated by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Service (IJAAS) as the Army Type 100 Heavy Bomber Model 1, it was known to the Allied by the reporting name "Helen".

ki67.name: Mitsubishi Ki-67
ki67.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi Ki-67 Hiryū , Allied reporting name "Peggy", was a twin-engine bomber produced by Mitsubishi Aircraft Company and used by the Imperial Japanese Army Air Service and Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service in World War II. While its original official designation was "Army Type 4 Heavy Bomber" , in all of its…

g4m.name: Mitsubishi G4M
g4m.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi G4M was a twin-engine, land-based medium bomber manufactured by the Mitsubishi Aircraft Company, a part of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, and operated by the Air Service (IJNAS) of the Imperial Japanese Navy from 1940 to 1945. Its official designation was Mitsubishi Navy Type 1 attack bomber  and was…

p1y.name: Yokosuka P1Y Ginga
p1y.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Yokosuka P1Y Ginga  is a twin-engine, land-based bomber that was designed by the Yokosuka Naval Air Technical Arsenal. Primarily produced by Nakajima and Kawanishi and flown by the Japanese Imperial Navy during the latter half of the Pacific War, it received the Allied reporting name “Frances”.

ki46.name: Mitsubishi Ki-46
ki46.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi Ki-46 is a twin-engine reconnaissance aircraft that was used by the Imperial Japanese Army in World War II. Its Army Shiki designation was Type 100 Command Reconnaissance Aircraft (一〇〇式司令部偵察機); the Allied brevity code name was "Dinah".

c6n.name: Nakajima C6N Saiun
c6n.credit: Unknown author / CC0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Nakajima C6N Saiun is a carrier-based reconnaissance aircraft designed and produced by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Nakajima Aircraft Company. Flown by the Imperial Japanese Navy Air Service (IJNAS) during World War II, the Allied reporting name was Myrt.

e13a.name: Aichi E13A
e13a.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Aichi E13A is a long-range reconnaissance seaplane designed and produced by the Japanese aviation company Aichi Kokuki KK. The Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) designation was "Navy Type 0 Reconnaissance Seaplane" (零式水上偵察機).

f1m.name: Mitsubishi F1M
f1m.credit: Imperial Japanese Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi F1M is a Japanese observation seaplane of World War II. It was the last biplane type of the Imperial Japanese Navy, with 944 built between 1936 and 1944.

h8k.name: Kawanishi H8K
h8k.credit: Max Smith / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawanishi H8K was a large four-engined flying boat designed and produced by the Japanese aviation manufacturer Kawanishi. The Imperial Japanese Navy (IJN) designation was "Type 2 Flying Boat" ; it was also referred to as "Type 2 Large-sized Flying Boat" , or "H2K flying boat" .

ki57.name: Mitsubishi Ki-57
ki57.credit: Charles M. Daniels / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Transport aircraft; Paratroop transport; Passenger aircraft
facts.about: The Mitsubishi Ki-57 was a Japanese passenger transport aircraft, developed from the Ki-21 bomber, during the early 1940s.

mig3.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-3
mig3.credit: Jno from http://www.aviation.ru/jno/ archive copy at the Wayback Machine / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.manufacturer: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG, Progress State Research and Production Rocket Space Center
facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-3 is a Soviet interceptor used during World War II. It was a development of the MiG-1 by the OKO of Zavod (Factory) No.

yak9.name: Yakovlev Yak-9
yak9.credit: Alf van Beem / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Yakovlev Yak-9 is a single-engine, single-seat multipurpose fighter aircraft used by the Soviet Union and its allies during World War II and the early Cold War. It was a development of the robust and successful Yak-7B fighter, which was based in turn on the tandem-seat advanced trainer known as the Yak-7UTI.

la5.name: Lavochkin La-5
la5.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lavochkin La-5 was a Soviet fighter aircraft of World War II. It was a development and refinement of the LaGG-3, replacing the earlier model's inline engine with the much more powerful Shvetsov ASh-82 radial engine.

il2.name: Ilyushin Il-2
il2.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Soviet ground attack aircraft of WWII
facts.about: The Ilyushin Il-2 is a ground-attack plane that was produced by the Soviet Union in large numbers during the Second World War. The word shturmovík, the generic Russian term for a ground-attack aircraft, became a synecdoche for the Il-2 in English sources, where it is commonly rendered Shturmovik, Stormovik and…

pe2.name: Petlyakov Pe-2
pe2.credit: U.S. Air Force photo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Petlyakov Pe-2 was a Soviet twin-engine dive bomber used during World War II. One of the outstanding tactical attack aircraft of the war, it also proved successful as a heavy fighter, as a night fighter and as a reconnaissance aircraft.

tu2.name: Tupolev Tu-2
tu2.credit: Gary Todd from Xinzheng, China / CC0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Tupolev Tu-2 is a twin-engined Soviet high-speed daylight and frontline bomber aircraft used during World War II. The Tu-2 was tailored to meet a requirement for a high-speed bomber or dive-bomber, with a large internal bomb load and speed similar to that of a single-seat fighter.

pe8.name: Petlyakov Pe-8
pe8.credit: SDASM Archives / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Petlyakov Pe-8 was a Soviet heavy bomber designed before World War II, and the only four-engine bomber the USSR built during the war. Produced in limited numbers, it was used to bomb Berlin in August 1941.

c130.name: Lockheed C-130 Hercules
c130.credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Tech. Sgt. Howard Blair / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed C-130 Hercules is an American, four-engined, turboprop, military transport aircraft designed and built by Lockheed. Capable of using unprepared runways for takeoffs and landings, the C-130 was designed as a troop, medical evacuation, and cargo transport aircraft.

kc135.name: Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker
kc135.credit: U.S. Air Force photo/Tech. Sgt. Angelique Perez / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: US military aerial refueling and transport aircraft
facts.role: Aerial refueling tanker and transport aircraft
facts.about: The Boeing KC-135 Stratotanker is an American military aerial refueling tanker aircraft that was developed from the Boeing 367-80 prototype, alongside the Boeing 707 airliner. It has a narrower fuselage and is shorter than the 707.

u2.name: Lockheed U-2
u2.credit: United States Department of the Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed U-2, nicknamed the "Dragon Lady", is an American single-engine, high–altitude reconnaissance aircraft operated by the United States Air Force (USAF) and the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) since the 1950s. Designed for all-weather, day-and-night intelligence gathering at altitudes above 70,000 feet,…

b52.name: Boeing B-52 Stratofortress
b52.credit: Airman 1st Class Victor J. Caputo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Boeing B-52 Stratofortress is an American nuclear-capable subsonic jet-powered strategic bomber. The B-52 was designed and built by Boeing, which has continued to provide support and upgrades.

tu95.name: Tupolev Tu-95
tu95.credit: Sergey Kustov / CC BY-SA 3.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Tupolev Tu-95 is a large Soviet nuclear-capable, four-engine turboprop strategic bomber and missile launch platform. First flown in 1952, the Tu-95 entered service with the Long-Range Aviation of the Soviet Air Forces in 1956 and was first used in combat in 2015.

vulcan.name: Avro Vulcan
vulcan.credit: Alastair Barbour / CC BY 2.5 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: British jet-powered delta wing strategic bomber
facts.about: The Avro Vulcan is a jet-powered, delta-wing, high-altitude strategic bomber, which was operated by the Royal Air Force (RAF) from 1956 until 1984. Aircraft manufacturer A.V. Roe and Company (Avro) designed the Vulcan in response to Specification B.35/46.

mig21.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21
mig21.credit: Gojanovic123456789 / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-21 is a supersonic jet fighter and interceptor aircraft, designed by the Mikoyan-Gurevich Design Bureau in the Soviet Union. Its nicknames include: "Balalaika", because its planform resembles the stringed musical instrument of the same name; "Ołówek", Polish for "pencil", due to the shape of…

f4.name: McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II
f4.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II is an American tandem two-seat, twin-engined, all-weather, long-range supersonic jet interceptor and fighter-bomber that was developed by McDonnell Aircraft for the United States Navy. It entered service with the Navy in 1961, then was adopted by the United States Marine Corps and…

uh1.name: Bell UH-1 Huey
uh1.credit: Airwolfhound from Hertfordshire, UK / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Huey family of American military utility helicopters
facts.about: The Bell UH-1 Iroquois is a utility military helicopter designed and produced by the American aerospace company Bell Helicopter. It is the first member of the prolific Huey family, as well as the first turbine-powered helicopter in service with the United States military.

ad-skyraider.name: Douglas A-1 Skyraider
ad-skyraider.credit: NASA Ames Research Center / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Douglas A-1 Skyraider is a single-seat attack aircraft designed and produced by American aerospace manufacturer Douglas Aircraft Company. It had an unusually long career, remaining in frontline service well into the Jet Age, thus becoming known by some as an "anachronism".

b36.name: Convair B-36 Peacemaker
b36.credit: U.S. Air Force photo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Convair B-36 "Peacemaker" was a piston-engined, strategic bomber built by Convair and operated by the United States Air Force's Strategic Air Command from 1948 to 1959. With 384 units built, the B-36 remains the largest mass-produced, piston-engined aircraft and has the longest wingspan of any combat aircraft.

f9f.name: Grumman F9F Panther
f9f.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Grumman F9F Panther is an early carrier-based jet fighter designed and produced by American aircraft manufacturer Grumman. It was the first jet-powered fighter aircraft to see air-to-air combat with the United States Navy, as well as being Grumman’s first jet fighter.

f84.name: Republic F-84 Thunderjet
f84.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Republic F-84 Thunderjet is an American turbojet fighter-bomber aircraft. Originating as a 1944 United States Army Air Forces (USAAF) proposal for a "day fighter", the F-84 first flew in 1946.

f86.name: North American F-86 Sabre
f86.credit: U.S. Air Force photo by J.M. Eddins Jr. / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The North American F-86 Sabre, sometimes called the Sabrejet, is a transonic, jet-powered fighter aircraft. Produced by North American Aviation, the Sabre is best known as the United States' first swept-wing fighter that could counter the swept-wing Soviet MiG-15 in high-speed dogfights in the skies of the Korean War…

b47.name: Boeing B-47 Stratojet
b47.credit: National Nuclear Security Administration / Nevada Site Office / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Boeing B-47 Stratojet is a retired American long-range, six-engined, turbojet-powered strategic bomber that was designed to fly at high subsonic speed and at high altitude to avoid enemy interceptor aircraft. The primary mission of the B-47 was as a nuclear bomber capable of striking targets within the Soviet…

f94.name: Lockheed F-94 Starfire
f94.credit: US Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed F-94 Starfire is a first-generation jet-powered all-weather day/night interceptor aircraft designed and produced by Lockheed Corporation. Put into production in 1949, it was the first operational United States Air Force (USAF) fighter equipped with an afterburner as well as being the first jet-powered…

t33.name: Lockheed T-33
t33.credit: Alejandro Pena; Edited by: FOX 52 and Bammesk / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed T-33 Shooting Star is a subsonic jet trainer designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Lockheed.

c119.name: Fairchild C-119 Flying Boxcar
c119.credit: U.S. Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Fairchild C-119 Flying Boxcar is an American military transport aircraft developed from the World War II-era Fairchild C-82 Packet, designed to carry cargo, personnel, litter patients, and mechanized equipment, and to drop cargo and troops by parachute. The first C-119 made its initial flight in November 1947,…

c124.name: Douglas C-124 Globemaster II
c124.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: American heavy lift military aircraft with 4 piston engines, 1946
facts.about: The Douglas C-124 Globemaster II, nicknamed "Old Shaky", is a retired American heavy-lift cargo aircraft built by the Douglas Aircraft Company in Long Beach, California.

hu16.name: Grumman HU-16 Albatross
hu16.credit: Dylan Agbagni / CC0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Grumman HU-16 Albatross is a twin-radial-engined, amphibious flying boat that was designed and produced by American aircraft manufacturer Grumman. Originally designated as the SA-16 in USAF service and the JR2F-1 and UF-1 in USN and USCG service, respectively, it was redesignated as the HU-16 in 1962.

h19.name: Sikorsky H-19 Chickasaw
h19.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Sikorsky H-19 Chickasaw is a multi-purpose piston-engined helicopter that was used by the United States Army and United States Air Force. It was also license-built by Westland Aircraft as the Westland Whirlwind in the United Kingdom.

h21.name: Piasecki H-21
h21.credit: US Army / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Piasecki H-21 Workhorse/Shawnee is an American helicopter, the fourth of a line of tandem rotor helicopters designed and built by Piasecki Helicopter. Commonly called "the flying banana", it was a multi-mission helicopter, capable of being fitted with wheels, skis or floats.

o1.name: Cessna O-1 Bird Dog
o1.credit: U.S. Army / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Cessna O-1 Bird Dog is a liaison and observation aircraft that first flew on December 14, 1949, and entered service in 1950 as the L-19 in the Korean War. It went on to serve in many branches of the U.S. Armed Forces, was not retired until the 1970s in a number of variants, and also served in the Vietnam War.

f2h.name: McDonnell F2H Banshee
f2h.credit: USN / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The McDonnell F2H Banshee is a single-seat carrier-based jet fighter aircraft designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer McDonnell Aircraft. It was an early jet fighter operated by United States Navy and United States Marine Corps, as well as being the only jet-powered fighter to ever be deployed by…

b57.name: Martin B-57 Canberra
b57.credit: United States Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: US license-built version of the British English Electric Canberra bomber
facts.about: The Martin B-57 Canberra is an American-built, twin-engined tactical bomber and reconnaissance aircraft that entered service with the United States Air Force (USAF) in 1953. The B-57 is a license-built version of the British English Electric Canberra, manufactured by the Glenn L. Martin Company.

a3.name: Douglas A-3 Skywarrior
a3.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Douglas A-3 Skywarrior is a jet-powered strategic bomber that was developed and produced by the Douglas Aircraft Company. It was designed by Douglas on behalf of the United States Navy, which sought a carrier-capable strategic bomber.

f100-super-sabre.name: North American F-100 Super Sabre
f100-super-sabre.credit: NASA / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The North American F-100 Super Sabre is an American supersonic jet fighter aircraft designed and produced by the aircraft manufacturer North American Aviation. The first of the Century Series of American jet fighters, it was the first United States Air Force (USAF) fighter capable of supersonic speed in level flight.

a4.name: Douglas A-4 Skyhawk
a4.credit: Lt.JG Nelson, U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Douglas A-4 Skyhawk is a single-seat, subsonic, carrier-capable, light attack aircraft designed and produced by American aerospace manufacturer Douglas Aircraft Company, later built by McDonnell Douglas. It was originally designated A4D under the United States Navy's pre-1962 designation system.

f101.name: McDonnell F-101 Voodoo
f101.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The McDonnell F-101 Voodoo is a supersonic jet fighter designed and produced by the American McDonnell Aircraft Corporation.

f102.name: Convair F-102 Delta Dagger
f102.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Cold War interceptor of the US Air Force
facts.about: The Convair F-102 Delta Dagger is an interceptor aircraft designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Convair. A member of the Century Series, the F-102 was the first operational supersonic interceptor and delta-wing fighter operated by the United States Air Force (USAF).

f104.name: Lockheed F-104 Starfighter
f104.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed F-104 Starfighter is an American single-engine, supersonic interceptor. Created as a day fighter by Lockheed as one of the "Century Series" of fighter aircraft for the United States Air Force (USAF), it was developed into an all-weather multirole aircraft in the early 1960s and extensively deployed as a…

f8.name: Vought F-8 Crusader
f8.credit: Jimmy Labianco / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Vought F-8 Crusader is a retired single-jet engine, supersonic, carrier-based air superiority fighter designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Vought. It was the last American fighter that had guns as the primary weapon, earning it the title "The Last of the Gunfighters".

f105.name: Republic F-105 Thunderchief
f105.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Republic F-105 Thunderchief is an American fighter-bomber that served with the United States Air Force from 1958 to 1984. Capable of Mach 2, it conducted the majority of strike bombing missions during the early years of the Vietnam War.

f106.name: Convair F-106 Delta Dart
f106.credit: Staff Sgt. John K. McDowell / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Convair F-106 Delta Dart is an all-weather interceptor aircraft designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Convair, a division of General Dynamics.

t37.name: Cessna T-37 Tweet
t37.credit: Staff Sgt. Andy Dunaway / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Cessna T-37 Tweet is a small, economical twin-engine jet trainer aircraft. It was flown for decades as a primary trainer of the United States Air Force (USAF) as well as in the air forces of several other nations.

ov1.name: Grumman OV-1 Mohawk
ov1.credit: U.S. Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Battlefield reconnaissance and forward air control aircraft
facts.about: The Grumman OV-1 Mohawk is an American armed military observation and attack aircraft that was designed for battlefield surveillance, light strike and transport capabilities. It features a twin turboprop configuration, and carries two crew members in side-by-side seating.

yak18.name: Yakovlev Yak-18
yak18.credit: Dmitry A. Mottl / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Training aircraft in the Soviet Union
facts.about: The Yakovlev Yak-18 is a tandem two-seat military primary trainer aircraft manufactured in the Soviet Union. Originally powered by one 119 kW (160 hp) Shvetsov M-11FR-1 radial piston engine, it entered service in 1946.

an2.name: Antonov An-2
an2.credit: Arpingstone / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Agricultural, utility aircraft and military transport aircraft
facts.about: The Antonov An-2  is a Soviet mass-produced single-engine biplane utility/agricultural aircraft designed and manufactured by the Antonov Design Bureau beginning in 1947. Its durability, lifting power, and ability to take off and land from poor runways have given it a long service life.

mi4.name: Mil Mi-4
mi4.credit: Jan Hrdonka / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mil Mi-4 is a Soviet transport helicopter that served in both military and civilian roles.

mig15.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15
mig15.credit: U.S. Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.manufacturer: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG, Progress State Research and Production Rocket Space Center
facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-15 is a single-seat transonic jet fighter aircraft developed by Mikoyan-Gurevich for the Soviet Union. The MiG-15 was one of the first successful jet fighters to incorporate swept wings to perform near Mach 1.

mig17.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17
mig17.credit: Balon Greyjoy / CC0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.manufacturer: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG, Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic
facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17 is a transonic fighter aircraft that was produced in the Soviet Union from 1952 and was operated by air forces internationally. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and in Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.

mig19.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19
mig19.credit: U.S. Air Force photo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19 is a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twinjet fighter aircraft. It was the first Soviet production aircraft capable of supersonic speeds in level flight.

il28.name: Ilyushin Il-28
il28.credit: Wisnia6522 / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.manufacturer: Знамя Труда (машиностроительный завод), Production Corporation Polyot
facts.about: The Ilyushin Il-28 is a medium-range jet bomber, originally manufactured for the Soviet Air Forces, in service since 1950. It was the Soviet Union's first such aircraft to enter large-scale production.

tu16.name: Tupolev Tu-16
tu16.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Tupolev Tu-16 is a twin-engined jet strategic heavy bomber used by the Soviet Union. It has been flown for almost 70 years.

m4.name: Myasishchev M-4
m4.credit: Unknown author / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Soviet strategic bomber and tanker aircraft
facts.about: The Myasishchev M-4 Molot was a four-engined strategic bomber designed by Vladimir Mikhailovich Myasishchev and manufactured by the Soviet Union in the 1950s to provide a Long Range Aviation bomber capable of attacking targets in North America.

an12.name: Antonov An-12
an12.credit: Igor Dvurekov / CC BY-SA 3.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Antonov An-12 is a four-engined turboprop cargo/military transport aircraft designed by Antonov and produced at the Irkutsk Aviation Plant and the Tashkent Mechanical Plant in the Soviet Union. It is a militarised version of the Antonov An-10 transport aircraft and was produced in many variants.

c5.name: Lockheed C-5 Galaxy
c5.credit: U.S. Air Force photo by Brett Snow / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed C-5 Galaxy is a large four-engine military transport aircraft designed and built by Lockheed Corporation, and now maintained and upgraded by its successor, Lockheed Martin. il76.name: Ilyushin Il-76
il76.credit: Ministry of Defence (Russia) / CC BY 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Russian heavy four-engined military transport jet aircraft
facts.about: The Ilyushin Il-76 is a multi-purpose, fixed-wing, four-engine turbofan strategic airlifter designed by the Soviet Union's Ilyushin design bureau as a commercial freighter in 1967, to replace the Antonov An-12. p3.name: Lockheed P-3 Orion
p3.credit: 海上自衛隊 / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

sr71.name: Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird
sr71.credit: USAF / Judson Brohmer / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Lockheed SR-71 "Blackbird" is a retired long-range, high-altitude, Mach 3+ strategic reconnaissance aircraft that was developed and manufactured by the American aerospace company Lockheed Corporation. Its nicknames include "Blackbird" and "Habu".

f14.name: Grumman F-14 Tomcat
f14.credit: U.S. Navy photo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

mig25.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25
mig25.credit: Peer.Gynt / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Family of interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft
facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-25 is a supersonic interceptor and reconnaissance aircraft that is among the fastest military aircraft to enter service. Designed by the Soviet Union's Mikoyan-Gurevich bureau, it is an aircraft built primarily using a nickel-steel alloy.

harrier.name: Harrier Jump Jet
harrier.credit: Javier Rodríguez from Palma de Mallorca, España / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Multirole combat aircraft family by Hawker Siddeley, later British Aerospace
facts.about: The Harrier, informally referred to as the Harrier jump jet, is a family of jet-powered attack aircraft capable of vertical/short takeoff and landing operations (V/STOL). Named after the bird of prey, it was originally developed by British manufacturer Hawker Siddeley in the 1960s.

viggen.name: Saab 37 Viggen
viggen.credit: Airwolfhound from Hertfordshire, UK / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: Saab 37 Viggen is a single-seat, single-engine multirole combat aircraft designed and produced by the Swedish aircraft manufacturer Saab. f5.name: Northrop F-5
f5.credit: Peng Chen / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Northrop F-5 is a family of supersonic light fighter aircraft initially designed as a privately funded project in the late 1950s by Northrop Corporation. There are two main models: the original F-5A and F-5B Freedom Fighter variants, and the extensively updated F-5E and F-5F Tiger II variants.

l39.name: Aero L-39 Albatros
l39.credit: Milan Nykodym / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Military trainer aircraft; Light ground-attack aircraft
facts.about: The Aero L-39 Albatros is a high-performance jet trainer designed and produced by Aero Vodochody in the Czech Republic. In addition to performing basic and advanced pilot training, it has also flown combat missions in a light-attack role.

t38.name: Northrop T-38 Talon
t38.credit: U.S. Department of Defense / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Military advanced trainer aircraft by Northrop
facts.about: The Northrop T-38 Talon is a two-seat, twinjet supersonic jet trainer designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer Northrop Corporation. It was the world's first supersonic trainer as well as the most produced.

ch47.name: Boeing CH-47 Chinook
ch47.credit: Sgt. Steven Galimore / CC0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: American tandem-rotor helicopter introduced in 1962 during the Cold War
facts.about: The Boeing CH-47 Chinook is a tandem-rotor helicopter originally developed by American rotorcraft company Vertol and now manufactured by Boeing Defense, Space & Security. The Chinook is the second-heaviest-lifting Western heavy-lift helicopter, behind the Sikorsky CH-53.

ch53.name: Sikorsky CH-53 Sea Stallion
ch53.credit: Staff Sgt. Raul Gonzalez, USMC / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The CH-53 Sea Stallion is a family of American heavy-lift transport helicopters designed and built by the American manufacturer Sikorsky Aircraft. ah1.name: Bell AH-1 Cobra
ah1.credit: US Army / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Bell AH-1 Cobra is a single-engined attack helicopter developed and manufactured by the American rotorcraft manufacturer Bell Helicopter. A member of the prolific Huey family, the AH-1 is also referred to as the HueyCobra or Snake.

mi24.name: Mil Mi-24

mi8.name: Mil Mi-8/17
mi8.credit: Igor Dvurekov / CC BY 3.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.manufacturer: Mil Moscow Helicopter Plant, Kazan Helicopters
facts.about: The Mil Mi-8 is a family of medium twin-turbine helicopters, originally designed by the Soviet Central Aerohydrodynamic Institute (TsAGI) in the 1960s and introduced into the Soviet Air Force in 1968. As of 2024, Russian production of the aircraft model continues.

b58.name: Convair B-58 Hustler
b58.credit: US Air Force / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Convair B-58 Hustler is a supersonic strategic bomber, the first capable of Mach 2 flight. Designed and produced by American aircraft manufacturer Convair, a division of General Dynamics, the B-58 was developed during the 1950s for the United States Air Force (USAF) Strategic Air Command (SAC).

sh3.name: Sikorsky SH-3 Sea King
sh3.credit: US Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.role: Anti-submarine warfare, search and rescue, transport and utility helicopter
facts.about: The Sikorsky SH-3 Sea King is an American twin-engine anti-submarine warfare (ASW) helicopter designed and built by Sikorsky Aircraft. A landmark design, it was one of the first ASW rotorcraft to use turboshaft engines.

a5.name: North American A-5 Vigilante
a5.credit: NASA Dryden Flight Research Center / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Cold War-era U.S. carrier-based supersonic bomber
facts.about: The North American A-5 Vigilante is an American carrier-based supersonic bomber and reconnaissance aircraft designed and built by North American Aviation (NAA) for the United States Navy. Before the 1962 unification of Navy and Air Force designations, it was designated A3J.

a6.name: Grumman A-6 Intruder
a6.credit: U.S. Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: 1960 attack strike aircraft family by Grumman

facts.about: The General Dynamics F-111 Aardvark is a retired, supersonic, medium-range fighter-bomber. Production models of the F-111 had roles that included attack, strategic bombing, reconnaissance, and electronic warfare.

a7.name: LTV A-7 Corsair II

facts.about: The LTV A-7 Corsair II is an American carrier-capable subsonic light attack aircraft designed and manufactured by Ling-Temco-Vought (LTV).

a37.name: Cessna A-37 Dragonfly

facts.about: The Cessna A-37 Dragonfly, or Super Tweet, is a jet-powered, light attack aircraft that was designed and produced by American aircraft manufacturer Cessna.

ov10.name: North American Rockwell OV-10 Bronco

facts.about: The North American Rockwell OV-10 Bronco is a twin-turboprop light attack and observation (O) aircraft with short takeoff and landing (V) capability designed and produced by the American aircraft manufacturer North American Rockwell. sh2.name: Kaman SH-2 Seasprite
sh2.credit: PH2 Wiggin, USN / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kaman SH-2 Seasprite is a ship-based helicopter originally developed and produced by American manufacturer Kaman Aircraft Corporation. It has been typically used as a compact and fast-moving rotorcraft for utility and anti-submarine warfare (ASW) missions.

hh3.name: Sikorsky HH-3 (S-61R)
hh3.credit: United States Coast Guard / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Sikorsky S-61R is a twin-engine helicopter used in transport or search and rescue roles. A developed version of the S-61, the S-61R was also built under license by Agusta as the AS-61R.

s3.name: Lockheed S-3 Viking
s3.credit: US Navy / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.description: Carrier-based anti-submarine and aerial refueling aircraft
facts.about: The Lockheed S-3 Viking is a four-crew, twin-engine turbofan-powered subsonic anti-submarine jet aircraft designed and produced by the American aerospace manufacturer Lockheed Corporation. ea6b.name: Grumman EA-6B Prowler
ea6b.credit: Cpl. Neysa Huertas Quinones / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Northrop Grumman EA-6B Prowler is a twin-engined, four-seat, mid-wing electronic-warfare aircraft. Operated by both the United States Marine Corps and United States Navy between 1971 and 2019, it was derived from the A-6 Intruder airframe.

kawasaki-c1.credit: Balon Greyjoy / CC0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Kawasaki C-1 is a twin-engined short-range military transport aircraft developed and manufactured by the Japanese conglomerate Kawasaki Heavy Industries. It was solely used by the Japan Air Self-Defense Force (JASDF).

mitsubishi-t2.name: Mitsubishi T-2
mitsubishi-t2.credit: Rob Schleiffert / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mitsubishi T-2 was a supersonic jet trainer aircraft designed and produced by the Japanese aerospace firm Mitsubishi. It was the first Japanese-developed aircraft to break the sound barrier.

facts.about: The Sukhoi Su-7 is a swept wing, supersonic fighter aircraft developed by the Soviet Union in 1955. Originally, it was designed as a tactical, low-level dogfighter, but was not successful in this role.

su15.name: Sukhoi Su-15
su15.credit: U.S. Department of Defense / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Sukhoi Su-15 is a twinjet supersonic interceptor aircraft developed by the Soviet Union. It entered service in 1965 and remained one of the front-line designs into the 1990s.

be12.name: Beriev Be-12

il38.name: Ilyushin Il-38
il38.credit: US Navy Employee / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

an26.name: Antonov An-26
an26.credit: Adrian Pingstone / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Antonov An-26 is a twin-engined turboprop regional airliner and military transport aircraft, designed and produced in the Soviet Union from 1969 to 1986. mig23.name: Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23
mig23.credit: DoD photo / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-23 is a single-engined, supersonic, variable-sweep wing fighter aircraft, designed by the Mikoyan-Gurevich design bureau in the Soviet Union. It is a third-generation jet fighter, alongside similar Soviet aircraft such as the Su-17 "Fitter".

su17.name: Sukhoi Su-17
su17.credit: SDASM / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Sukhoi Su-17 is a variable-sweep wing fighter-bomber developed for the Soviet military. Developed from the Sukhoi Su-7, the Su-17 was the first variable-sweep wing aircraft to enter Soviet service and featured updated avionics.

su24.name: Sukhoi Su-24
su24.credit: U.S. Department of Defense / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Sukhoi Su-24 is a supersonic, all-weather tactical bomber developed in the Soviet Union. The aircraft has a variable-sweep wing, twin engines and a side-by-side seating arrangement for its crew of two.

an225.name: Antonov An-225 Mriya
an225.credit: Myroslav Kaplun / CC BY-SA 4.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Antonov An-225 Mriya was a large strategic airlift cargo aircraft designed and produced by the Antonov Design Bureau in the Soviet Union.

facts.manufacturer: Boeing Defense, Space & Security, Westinghouse Electric Corporation
facts.about: The Boeing E-3 Sentry is an American airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft developed by Boeing. E-3s are commonly known as AWACS.

b1.name: Rockwell B-1 Lancer
b1.credit: USAF / Public domain / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Rockwell B-1 Lancer is a supersonic variable-sweep wing heavy bomber used by the United States Air Force. It has been nicknamed the "Bone".

tu160.credit: Alex Beltyukov / CC BY-SA 3.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Tupolev Tu-160 is a Soviet/Russian nuclear-capable supersonic, variable-sweep wing heavy strategic bomber and airborne missile platform designed by the Tupolev Design Bureau in the 1970s. tu22m.credit: Dmitry Terekhov from Odintsovo, Russian Federation / CC BY-SA 2.0 / via Wikimedia Commons

facts.about: The Tupolev Tu-22M is a Soviet nuclear capable, supersonic, variable-sweep wing, long-range strategic and maritime strike bomber developed by the Tupolev Design Bureau in the 1960s. The bomber was reported as being designated Tu-26 by Western intelligence at one time.

mirage2000.name: Dassault Mirage 2000

f117.name: Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk
